title: Nuclear Chemistry
seo_title: Nuclear Chemistry Worksheets: Radioactive Decay, Half-Life, Fission and Fusion (Chemistry)
standard_text: Develop models to illustrate the changes in the composition of the nucleus of the atom and the energy released during the processes of fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on nuclear chemistry (NGSS HS-PS1-8): alpha, beta and gamma decay, nuclear equations, half-life, fission and fusion. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Decay, fission and fusion change protons and neutrons and release huge energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Nuclear changes alter the nucleus, so one element can become another.

  • Alpha (42He): mass −4, atomic number −2. Beta (electron): atomic number +1, mass same. Gamma: energy only.
  • Half-life: after n half-lives, (1/2)n of the sample is left.
  • Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion joins light nuclei. Both turn a little mass into a lot of energy.
Example

23892U alpha decay?

238 − 4, 92 − 2

Answer: 23490Th

Example

80 g, 3 half-lives. Left?

80 → 40 → 20 → 10

Answer: 10 g

Common mistakes

  • Thinking beta decay lowers the mass number.
  • Thinking nothing is left after two half-lives.
  • Mixing up fission (split) and fusion (join).

faq.q: How do alpha and beta decay change a nucleus?
faq.a: Alpha decay lowers the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2. Beta decay raises the atomic number by 1 and keeps the mass number the same.

faq.q: How do you solve half-life problems?
faq.a: Find how many half-lives have passed (time ÷ half-life) and halve the amount that many times.

faq.q: What is the difference between fission and fusion?
faq.a: Fission splits a heavy nucleus into smaller ones. Fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one. Both release large amounts of energy.
